key_insight: Physics-guided deep learning reconstructs bubble depth and physical-equivalent diameter from single-camera shadowgraphs without stereoscopic hardware.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a scalable way to measure bubble size and spatial distribution governing transport and uniformity in dense multiphase flows.
method: Render DNS-resolved bubbles at multiple focal planes using validated Monte Carlo ray tracing.
Preprocess labeled images and split data by DNS timestamp to prevent leakage.
Predict signed depth and diameter with a focus-conditioned multitask network.
evidence_signal: Using 900 frames and 87,728 labeled instances, the model achieved ~97.6% normalized depth accuracy on held-out data; a 180-bubble closed-loop test yielded diameter error below 9.71%, while experimental diameter-PDF overlap ranged from 68% to 92%.
watch_item: Reconstruction errors increase with distance from the focal plane, imposing a recoverability limit that must be characterized for deployment.
paper_title: Monocular 3D bubble reconstruction: DNS-informed ray tracing and deep learning
